questions.scenario: A patient with a pruritic vulvar plaque undergoes biopsy. The section includes the surface epithelium and underlying tissue.
questions.lead_in: Which arrangement of the abnormal cells is visible in the biopsy?
questions.stem: Which arrangement of the abnormal cells is visible in the biopsy?
options: Large pale cells dispersed among epidermal keratinocytes
Thin epidermis over a band of superficial dermal sclerosis
Exophytic squamous papillae with koilocytic atypia
A circumscribed dermal nodule with complex papillary glands
Immature basaloid cells replacing the upper squamous layers
choice_rationales: The pale cells interrupt the usual darker keratinocyte population within the epidermis.
A thin epidermis and sclerotic dermis would favor lichen sclerosus. Here the striking abnormality is within the epithelium.
Condyloma has outward branching stromal cores and koilocytes. This surface lacks that exophytic architecture.
Papillary hidradenoma forms a separate dermal glandular nodule. The pale cells here lie among keratinocytes.
Classic vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia shows impaired squamous maturation with basaloid cells extending upward. Here the conspicuous cells are large and pale.
questions.explanation: Scan the purple epidermis beneath the surface. Large pale atypical cells are interspersed among darker keratinocytes.
visual_clues: The epidermis is the darker band along the top.
Several pale cells are larger than the adjacent keratinocytes.
questions.visual_target: Pale atypical cells in the epidermis

Extramammary Paget disease
Condyloma acuminatum
Papillary hidradenoma
Classic vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia
choice_rationales: Expect epithelial thinning with superficial dermal sclerosis rather than this pale intraepidermal cell population.
Large pale malignant cells scattered within the vulvar epidermis are the pattern described for Paget disease.
Expect exophytic fibrovascular papillae covered by koilocytic squamous epithelium.
Expect a circumscribed dermal tumor with a complex papillary glandular pattern and no epidermal connection.
Expect atypical immature basaloid squamous cells and loss of maturation toward the surface, rather than scattered large pale cells.
questions.explanation: The large pale intraepidermal cells support extramammary Paget disease. The lecture describes its plaque as potentially eczema like and notes that cytoplasmic mucin staining can help confirm the diagnosis.
visual_clues: Use the level of the atypical cells and their pale cytoplasm together.
